Header: Cnaphalocrocis medinalis Sinhala - Kola hakulana dalabuwa, Tamil - Ilaimadichikkatti

Prevention: If high infestation occurred in previous season, plough the land just after harvesting.
Remove shade around the field, better at the beginning of the season.
Establishment of crop at a correct time of season:
Use recommended seed rate i.e. 40 to 50 kg per acre.
Use recommended fertilizer based on leaf colour chart.
Remove grassy weeds time to time in crop and surroundings.
Those weeds act as alternative host plants.
Avoid unnecessary pesticide application to conserve natural enemies.
Monitoring: Observe the field for leaf folder damage from tillering to flowering.
Observe damaged leaves and availability of live larvae inside folded leaves.
When infestation is high, leaf folder moth can also be observed
Randomly select 10 hills in a 500 m 2 area.
If 10 larvae are observed and 25% of leaves are damaged, then an insecticide has to be applied for chemical control
Direct Control: When the damage appears as patches in the beginning remove the damaged leaves along with larvae and destroy.
Restrictions: Spot application of recommended insecticide at the beginning of damage symptoms will also help to conserve natural enemies.
